title: Show-brand typography family
slide_intent: Demonstrate variation within a shared type system, because programme identities need individual character while remaining connected to their broadcaster.
strategic_value: Different widths, weights and treatments can give Channel 4 shows distinct tones without relying on wholly unrelated lettering systems.
demonstration: A three-by-three grid on dark backgrounds compares title treatments for It’s a Sin, Derry Girls, Paralympics, Formula 1, True Crime, Taskmaster, The Windsors, Hollyoaks and deceit.
practical_value: Compare how width, weight, spacing and arrangement change a programme title’s voice.

content_islands.name: Title grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange nine white programme names in three rows, preserving each title’s distinct width, weight and alignment.

content_islands.name: Treatment labels
content_islands.spec: Retain the small style labels above each specimen as part of the comparison; do not infer rules from unreadable fine values.

reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram’s accompanying case study explains that show assets should align with the masterbrand while retaining appropriate tonal flexibility.
reference_purposes.Expression: A three-by-three grid on dark backgrounds compares title treatments for It’s a Sin, Derry Girls, Paralympics, Formula 1, True Crime, Taskmaster, The Windsors, Hollyoaks and deceit.
reference_purposes.Application: The source demonstrates this treatment in nine programme-title treatments.
